The producer corrected this during review in its new step 6.1. findings.location: Pre-reader Proof step 5.3, “since the base stars form a basis”
findings.evidence: Fixed finite simplex open stars do not form a basis for the ordinary topology: an edge-interior star cannot refine small intervals around an interior point. Agreement on those stars alone therefore does not establish the derived sheaf comparison. A cofinal small-ball acyclicity calculation closes this short omission. The producer supplied that calculation and the termwise comparison during review. This finding preserves historical evidence bound to the observed pre-reader bytes.

The construction emits smooth algebraically irreducible strata, but the defining convention requires connected strata in the analytic topology. The algebraic dimension and regular-locus suppliers and local holomorphic charts do not establish global analytic connectedness. Supply a locally proved connectedness comparison or an alternative finite connected-stratum construction. [Milne, Chapter 15, Proposition 15.1](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AG15.pdf) confirms the comparison statement but defers its general proof to Shafarevich VII.2, which was not recovered here. The unchanged theorem remains present for Step 3b.
